written.question:
A non-periodic composite signal is formed by combining five sinusoidal components with frequencies of 0 Hz, 4 Hz, 8 Hz, 12 Hz and 16 Hz. The two terminal frequency components have peak amplitudes of 3 V and 5 V respectively, while the center frequency component has a peak amplitude of 20 V.
(i) Determine the bandwidth of the composite signal. [1]
(ii) Sketch the frequency-domain representation of the signal, clearly indicating the bandwidth. [2]
(iii) Now assume the signal is periodic and draw the revised frequency-domain representation. [1]

items.label: Continuous curve (not spikes) from 0 to 16 Hz
Amplitudes 3 V at 0 Hz, 20 V at 8 Hz, 5 V at 16 Hz marked
Bandwidth 16 Hz indicated with an arrow

rubric.modelAnswer: (i) B = fh − fl = 16 − 0 = 16 Hz. (ii) Continuous spectrum 0–16 Hz: 3 V at 0 Hz, peak 20 V at 8 Hz, 5 V at 16 Hz; B = 16 Hz marked. (iii) Periodic → five discrete spikes at 0, 4, 8, 12, 16 Hz (3 V, unspecified, 20 V, unspecified, 5 V).

written.question: Distinguish between the frequency-domain representations of periodic and nonperiodic composite signals.

rubric.modelAnswer: By Fourier analysis, a periodic composite signal decomposes into sine waves with discrete frequencies, so its frequency domain shows separate spikes. A nonperiodic composite signal decomposes into sine waves with continuous frequencies, so its frequency domain is a continuous curve over a range (e.g. speech).
